races.name: Glass Times EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Flat Out Flat Glass Solutions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who posted a good recent win over 7f on soft, identical conditions to today; trainer Margarson only 1/7 last 14 days and the horse carries a hood, suggesting management of a quirky profile — needs pace to chase down.|

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: sole confirmed front-runner who won over 7f on soft last time and knows how to dictate; 56 days off is a minor query but Simon Dow fires 2/8 in the past fortnight and this looks set up around her strengths.|

runners_data.name: Uppercase
runners_data.note: Progressive 4-year-old who has won twice this season including a 7f soft success — excellent course-condition fit; Harry Eustace has not fired a winner in 17 attempts over 14 days so the trainer is quiet, but the horse's form profile suits this shape perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner by history but recent form shows beaten well in similar fields; hood fitted, and the similar-going record (0W0P from one run) is a concern — likely to race prominently but no obvious winning thread in this company.|

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted prominent type with a recent 2nd on soft and a win over this trip in good ground; Eve Johnson Houghton flying with 3/36 in 14 days and the horse's profile sits comfortably in the box seat behind Musical Angel.|

runners_data.name: Cuban Lady
runners_data.note: Sharp form at 6f placed at 2nd and 3rd on good ground in good company; her natural instinct is to race from behind, but with multiple closers in this field she is likely pushed into a midfield berth, making it harder to produce her usual finishing move.|

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on a strong winning streak — three wins in last six and a fine 2nd over 7f on good — races from a hold-up position but with natural class and Cieren Fallon in the saddle; Epsom debut is an unknown but the form demands respect.|

runners_data.name: Galileo Island
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has shown best form at 7f and was placed over this trip on good; the 68-day absence is the headline concern and Tom Ward's 1/22 fortnight strike rate adds little confidence to this being a readiness run.|

runners_data.name: Euphonia
runners_data.note: Won twice from seven starts including a soft-ground 7f success, suggesting the conditions are fine; however, this horse is a natural closer whose best chance requires a truly run race — bumped forward into midfield by the congested hold-up division, its chance is materially softened in a slowly-run shape.|

races.paceDynamic: Musical Angel is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, she is likely to control this 7f Epsom contest from the front at a measured, self-dictated tempo on Good to Soft ground. Silver Trumpet and Uppercase will press forward from a prominent pitch and could sit just behind Musical Angel, giving the race a compact early order rather than a true gallop, which on this track and going favours those who travel well into the race rather than those who need a strongly-run test. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Cuban Lady and Euphonia are genuine closers who are expected to be bumped forward into midfield positions rather than racing from their preferred rear berth, which blunts their late-running threat. This race shape — a measured pace set by one front-runner with prominent types tracking close — clearly favours prominent racers and those who can make a forward move from just off the pace before the short Epsom straight, rather than true hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel sets a sustainable pace unchallenged and the race develops as a test of cruising speed rather than stamina.
scenarios.body: Musical Angel dictates from the front and the proximity of Silver Trumpet and Uppercase keeps the pace honest without burning them off; the winner emerges from the lead or first pursuit group entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Nabbed
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel's tempo proves too slow and a prominent chaser produces a sustained run to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Silver Trumpet or Uppercase, sitting just off the pace, finds the good-to-soft ground to their liking and picks off Musical Angel as she ties up late; the winner is one who saved a fraction of energy while still racing prominently.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Succeed
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel sets a genuinely hot early tempo from the front and the race develops into a true stamina test on soft ground.
scenarios.body: The strong pace burns off the prominent types and creates a genuine closing run from midfield, allowing Norcross Brow or Dapper Guest to reel in the leaders late; this scenario requires the pace to be faster than Musical Angel typically sets it, making it conditional.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Cuban Lady or Euphonia secure a truly wide, unimpeded run from their rearward position and produce a finishing burst that overcomes their compromised starting point.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because both horses are redistibuted from their natural hold-up role into midfield and are unlikely to get the true strong gallop they need to close ground; even if the pace is strong, they face a disadvantaged trip around Epsom.

watchPoints.text: Musical Angel's early tempo is the race pivot — if she dawdles in front unchallenged, Silver Trumpet and Uppercase are the primary threats to reel her in before the line; watch whether Harry Davies allows the pace to drift.

Cuban Lady and Euphonia are likely to be ridden from positions further forward than ideal for both — any crowding or lack of cover in the early stages could compromise their races before the straight is even reached.

Norcross Brow's form figures are striking but all five recent runs are on good ground; today's Good to Soft at Epsom is a first soft-surface test and the jump in ground softness is worth watching closely early.

Galileo Island is 68 days absent with a trainer firing at 1/22 in the last fortnight — if it travels poorly or hangs early, discount it; but a prominent horse returning fresh on good-to-soft that takes to it could outrun a big price.

Isobelle Chalmers takes off 7lb on Cuban Lady, which is a useful weight pull — watch whether the reduced burden allows the filly to travel more freely than mapped, potentially putting her closer than her natural style suggests.

races.name: Chigwell Group - The Trade's Front Runner Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Moonrunner
runners_data.note: Soft-ground form is solid (placed twice over 12f on soft), Charlie Fellowes runner returning after 19 days at a trip that suits; naturally a hold-up horse but sits closest to the pace in this configuration, meaning Kaiya Fraser can track Bobacious without fighting for position — the most naturally placed closer in the race.

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Jack Callan takes the ride for Dylan Cunha, with a good recent record (2nd on soft over 10f) and three placings from five starts at 12f on good or better; visor-wearer whose best soft form puts him in the frame, though he is a true hold-up type who will need gaps to open in the straight.

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave is a significant booking for Jim Boyle, who sends this five-year-old out just 13 days after its last run; all recent form has come on good ground and there is a soft-ground question mark — one win and two places in six attempts on similar going is workable but not dominant, and the step back to 12f is the trip on which it finished 4th most recently.

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: William Knight has been firing in winners at 5/14 in the 14-day window and Hector Crouch is an astute pilot; genuinely a hold-up horse placed into a midfield slot here simply because the field is stacked with closers — its soft-ground record is limited (1W1P from four attempts on good) and the style fit of 0.93 suggests it will struggle to reproduce its best racing out of its comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Skibo
runners_data.note: Barry Brennan's charge has shown improvement on good ground (placed twice at 10f) but only one run in seven on any going comparable to today's soft; a true hold-up type pushed into midfield by the shape of this race, and the style-fit concern (0.91) is real — Tyler Heard will need a trouble-free trip and a strong pace to make this work.

runners_data.name: Barry's Boy
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley sends out a horse whose sole win came over 8f on standard ground, and whose six-runner form string includes a distant sixth and ninth in recent outings; a hold-up horse reclassified to midfield here, carrying 132lbs and making its soft-ground and 10f debut simultaneously — trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/9 adds no confidence.

runners_data.name: Thankyou Baroness
runners_data.note: Mrs Gansera-Leveque's five-year-old has one win on good at 12f and placed on soft over the same trip, which is the most relevant positive; the alarming flag is 195 days off the track, and while Benoit de la Sayette is an elite jockey booking, the lengthy absence makes fitness the primary concern — naturally a hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield role by the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon is a high-quality jockey booking for James Owen (2/33 in 14 days) and this horse carries hood and tongue-tie; only one run in fifteen on soft ground and all recent form has been on good, which is a genuine going concern, and the style-fit tag (0.93) confirms it will be racing out of its natural hold-up role in today's shape.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and the pivotal pace-setter — Mark Hoad's six-year-old won over 10f on good and was placed on soft, and Liam Wright (claiming 3lb) inherits a race shape that could not suit better; the only question is whether its form figures (1 win from 15 soft-ground attempts) represent a genuine soft-ground limitation or small-sample noise.

runners_data.name: Yokkell
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's seven-year-old returns after 47 days off (the longest layoff in the field) and George Wood takes the ride; has won over 12f on firm and placed at Epsom on good ground, but soft-going form is sparse and the layoff combined with a hold-up style pushed into midfield means it faces multiple overlapping problems on race day.

races.paceDynamic: Bobacious is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of ten and, with no rival willing or able to press them, Liam Wright's mount should dictate terms at whatever tempo suits on Good To Soft ground over 1m2f at Epsom. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up horses — Moonrunner, Patrol, Carnival Day, Beach Point, Skibo, Barry's Boy, Thankyou Baroness, Super Hit, and Yokkell all prefer to race off the pace — which means Bobacious will face zero early pressure and can control the fractions entirely. This race shape strongly favours horses capable of tracking the leader in a compressed midfield or those with a powerful sustained finish, because the pace will be honest but controlled rather than truly searching on this testing ground. The field holds far more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Beach Point, Skibo, Barry's Boy, Thankyou Baroness, Super Hit, and Yokkell are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, and it is Moonrunner, Patrol, and Carnival Day — the horses naturally placed closest to the pace — who are most likely to actually secure the tactical positions that matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bobacious Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged and sets a controlled, measured pace that burns off the closers.
scenarios.body: Bobacious finds the perfect race-in-running from a soft lead on Good To Soft ground, with no rival capable of applying early pressure and the hold-up brigade forced to make their move from further back than ideal; horses who can travel prominently close to the leader and produce a sustained effort into the straight will have the clearest run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground slows the pace enough that horses tracking Bobacious from second or third quicken through in the straight.
scenarios.body: The controlled tempo set by Bobacious plays into the hands of Moonrunner and Patrol, who sit within a few lengths and can utilise their soft-ground form when the tempo lifts in the final two furlongs; Carnival Day, returning from only 13 days off with Pat Cosgrave aboard, could also make a forward move having been placed on similar ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true hold-up horse produces a devastating late run.
scenarios.body: This is structurally unlikely given how many redistributed hold-up types will be fighting for wide positions with no clear path through — Beach Point and Super Hit have the profiles but start at a positional disadvantage having been pushed out of their natural roles; if ground conditions extract a strong gallop from Bobacious and the leaders tie up, one of the redistributed closers could emerge, but the congested midfield makes this a low-probability route.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up types make premature moves racing wide, disrupting the field and turning the race into an attritional contest.
scenarios.body: With so many horses out of their natural position — Skibo, Barry's Boy, Thankyou Baroness all genuine hold-up types who must race in an unnatural midfield — a messy, strung-out race on soft ground could suit the most adaptable stayer; Barry's Boy won over 8f on standard ground and steps up markedly in trip here, while Thankyou Baroness has a soft-ground win at 12f but is 195 days off.

watchPoints.text: Bobacious is the sole pace-setter — if Liam Wright (claiming 3lb) goes too slow on the soft ground and allows a cluster of hold-up horses to coast into contention turning for home, the race could be decided by a late sprint that Bobacious cannot match.

Beach Point, Skibo, Barry's Boy, Thankyou Baroness, Super Hit, and Yokkell are all genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield — watch for traffic congestion and wide sweeping moves in the straight as multiple closers hunt the same ground simultaneously.

Thankyou Baroness is 195 days off the track — monitor in the paddock for signs of fitness and monitor Benoit de la Sayette's riding instructions; a stale horse with a top jockey is a volatile combination that could go very well or not fire at all.

Pat Cosgrave on Carnival Day is a booking worth tracking at the off — Cosgrave rides regularly for Jim Boyle and tends to be placed on horses with realistic each-way claims; all of Carnival Day's form is on good ground, so watch the going board for any drying between now and race time.

William Knight's 14-day strike rate of 5/14 is the most compelling trainer angle in the race — Beach Point is the beneficiary, and while its positional redistribution is a concern, Knight runners in form at this kind of strike rate deserve monitoring regardless of the pace map disadvantage.

races.name: Quickslide Quick Ride Apprentices' Derby Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Charmaine
runners_data.note: Five-year-old trained by Fanshawe who races prominently and has solid soft-ground form; placed on similar going last time, her stats in analogous conditions are encouraging (1 place from 15 runs) and the step back up to 12f-plus suits her profile well — Arron D'Arcy (7lb claim) keeps the weight low.

runners_data.name: Gordon Grey
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, wearing a tongue-tie and fitted with a hood; his soft-ground record is modest (one place from 15 runs) and he has been beaten far out of the frame at this level recently, meaning his role as pace-setter is more likely to set up the race for others than to win it himself.

runners_data.name: Galaxy Star
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old for Alan King who has won at a similar level on Standard ground and handles soft variants — his Trainer 14-day record (1 from 12) is modest, but Harry Vigors's 3lb claim helps, and the prominent style suits a race where the pace is expected to be controlled.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse wearing a tongue-tie whose best form has come over shorter trips on Good ground; soft ground experience is limited (no wins or places from two runs on similar), and coming from off a steady pace over 1m4f at Epsom is a demanding ask, though Toby Moore (5lb) keeps the burden light.

runners_data.name: Naval Command
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Ralph Beckett returning after 56 days off, with one soft-ground outing on record and no wins or places on that surface; the trip is within range but the lack of any meaningful form on a soft surface and the wide layoff make him a speculative each-way interest at best.

runners_data.name: Duc De Kent
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old is a natural hold-up type whose form figures of 590/60 underline a horse who rarely threatens on the day; pushed into a midfield map position because the field's genuine hold-up contingent outnumbers available rear slots — racing out of his preferred position further tempers his claims, and the STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 reflects a real discounting of his chance in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Crooked Path
runners_data.note: Progressive four-year-old who has won twice in his last four starts including on soft ground and over 12f on Standard — Mason Paetel takes over in the saddle and the prominent style fits perfectly in a race where Gordon Grey will give him a target; strong each-way profile given the soft-ground experience (12 from 15 on similar going) and the relatively low weight of 125lbs.

races.paceDynamic: Gordon Grey is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to press from the front in a field of seven, he is likely to set a controlled, measured gallop over this 1m4f on Good To Soft ground at Epsom. Charmaine, Galaxy Star, and Crooked Path are all prominent types who will want to track close to the pace, creating a compact early order behind Gordon Grey rather than a true battle for the lead. The soft-ish ground will further suppress early tempo, meaning Gordon Grey can dictate without being pressured and the race is likely to develop into a stamina-testing grind in the home straight rather than a sprint finish. This shape most strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with genuine stamina who can travel smoothly into a steady pace and pick off a front-runner who has had things his own way — horses like Charmaine and Crooked Path, who have course-appropriate profiles, are in the prime tactical position. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Duc De Kent is a genuine hold-up horse who is mapped to midfield due to redistribution, while Naval Command and Epictetus are the true closers — those two are best placed to finish off the race from off the pace if the front group do not go hard enough to soften themselves up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gordon Grey Controls Softly
scenarios.trigger: If Gordon Grey leads unchallenged at a steady pace and the prominent trio track him into the straight.
scenarios.body: Gordon Grey's uncontested lead on soft ground turns the race into a test of who can sustain their gallop longest, and the horse who settles best just off him has a decisive advantage; Charmaine and Crooked Path, both comfortable in prominent positions, are ideally placed to pounce when Gordon Grey's effort ebbs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the steady early pace allows one of the prominent horses to pick up powerfully from the home turn and go clear before closers can respond.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop means the race is not stamina-sapping enough to neutralise a horse with a decisive turn of foot; Galaxy Star, who has won off his current mark and handles soft variants, could be that horse if he travels with cover behind Gordon Grey.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the outset to soften up the front and prominent runners, allowing hold-up horses to come through late.
scenarios.body: Gordon Grey would need to push harder than his recent form suggests likely, but if that happens Epictetus and Naval Command, both genuine hold-up types, have the profile to pick up the pieces; Epictetus has shown ability on this surface and could be the most dangerous closer if the pace truly develops.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Collapses Field
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground bites hard and the race turns into an attritional grind that stops them all, with the horse in the best physical condition on the day winning close home.
scenarios.body: This scenario is unlikely given the going is borderline Good To Soft rather than heavy, but Naval Command, with proven stamina over today's trip and soft experience, would be the beneficiary if it gets truly gruelling; Duc De Kent's redistribution means his position is unnatural and he is unlikely to feature even in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gordon Grey's early demeanour — if Jack Callan elects to take a stronger hold and back off the pace rather than bowl along in front, there is no horse in this field with an obvious desire to make the running, which could create an uncharacteristic slow crawl and a chaotic sprint finish.

Crooked Path's soft-ground record (12 from 15 runs on similar going with a win and eight places) stands out markedly in this field — if the pace develops as expected and he gets a clear run from prominent, his form profile is significantly better suited to conditions than his odds may reflect.

Duc De Kent is mapped to midfield but is a genuine hold-up type racing out of role — if he is restrained toward the rear as natural instinct dictates, he will be covering significantly more ground than rivals on Epsom's unique undulating track and will need an unusually strong finish to compensate.

Galaxy Star has won at a similar standard and age profile, but his trainer's 14-day strike rate of just 1 from 12 is worth noting — not a strong handler flag but worth monitoring in the market to see if stable confidence is reflected in support.

The going report shows the card is running consistently Good To Soft across all distances — no drift toward heavier conditions has been flagged, which slightly favours the front and prominent runners over the pure hold-up horses who need a genuinely testing surface to maximise their finishing bursts.

races.name: Under Starters Orders For Fit Show 2027 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Virtue Diligence
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up filly with a sim-going win last time (1/6), trainer Perrett with no 14-day wins from 8; the 1m4f trip is a slight stretch on form but not disqualifying, and she could be value at a bigger price if the pace quickens.|

runners_data.name: Sullom Voe
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant concern in a 17-runner staying handicap — Menuisier runner without a 14-day win, and back-to-back eighths suggest this is a tough puzzle to solve even with soft-ground conditions.|

runners_data.name: Flag Of Eva
runners_data.note: Appleby has been in decent form (3 wins from 26 over 14 days), and this filly has two placed efforts from five at 10f-11f on good ground; the step to 1m4f on softer ground is a new question but the form trajectory is quietly solid.|

runners_data.name: Shirakawa
runners_data.note: The single confirmed pace-setter in the race — Eve Johnson Houghton sends her in with three 14-day winners from 36, and the horse's own record shows back-to-back wins at 10f on good ground before a below-par effort at 12f on an artificial surface; today's soft turf at 1m4f is a fresh surface question, but the tactical advantage of leading unchallenged is substantial.|

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type, Queally up, and a 9/7f-race record suggesting the step to 1m4f on soft is ambitious; the sim-going strike rate is modest (0W1P from 15) and the trainer has only one runner in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Has a placed effort at 1m4f on good ground and won at 1m2f, so the trip appears within range; trainer Flood has no 14-day wins from a single runner, and the form string of 150124 shows she can be inconsistent — raw ability is there but the race shape doesn't set her up ideally as a deep closer.|

runners_data.name: Tenison
runners_data.note: Chapple-Hyam sends this horse in with genuine soft-ground form including a win at 1m2f on soft — though his true style is hold-up, the map places him mid-division given the overcrowded rear; the STYLE_FIT of 0.91 means he won't be in his ideal spot, but the soft-ground credentials are real.|

runners_data.name: Blue Hill
runners_data.note: De la Sayette takes the mount on this prominent racer for Ismail Mohammed & Jose Santos — three runs all in the 5th range, and the consistent form suggests he is placed to run his race without threatening the principals; the 1m4f on soft is untested territory.|

runners_data.name: Eze Sur Mer
runners_data.note: Returned after 98 days off, which is the longest absence in the field — Newland & Insole have one win from 14 over 14 days, and the horse's recent record shows five consecutive finishes between 4th and 12th; the redistribution to mid-division means he's not in his preferred deep hold-up spot, compounding an already difficult ask.|

runners_data.name: Caraway
runners_data.note: Haggas and Fallon is a high-quality combination, and the horse has two wins and multiple placed efforts at distances between 12f and 14f; a genuine hold-up horse placed in mid-division by necessity, the STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects the positional compromise, but raw ability gives this runner the best realistic claim among the redistribution group.|

runners_data.name: Time To Sparkle
runners_data.note: Has a win at 10f on standard and multiple placed efforts at similar trips — natural prominent racer who should find a comfortable position just off Shirakawa, and James Keane's runner has run 153231 recently suggesting consistent competitiveness without winning at this level.|

runners_data.name: Darkest Red
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle runner with Cosgrave aboard — four placed efforts in the last five including two seconds at 12f, one on soft; a genuine stayer pushed away from his preferred deep position by the redistribution, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 limits expectations, but the ground suits and the form at staying trips is encouraging.|

runners_data.name: Antiquarian
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore send this one in with a form string of 5-600 and two 10th-place finishes on AW — the redistribution to mid-division compounds what is already a difficult profile, and the absence of any meaningful placed effort makes this hard to support.|

runners_data.name: Eshowe
runners_data.note: Three runs, all on artificial surfaces producing 11th, 10th and 12th — no turf form, no soft-ground form, flagged for fading in the finish, and redistributed to mid-division despite being a hold-up type; this is a very difficult race for a horse of this profile.|

runners_data.name: Dijon Gone
runners_data.note: A second at 1m2f on soft (2/12f/SOF) is the standout in an otherwise modest record — redistribution away from his natural hold-up position is a genuine handicap, but the soft-ground evidence and a recent run 12 days ago mean condition is not the concern; trip stamina at 1m4f is the question.|

runners_data.name: Fletcher
runners_data.note: Won at 1m2f on good and has three placed efforts at 12f — Jim Boyle's second string behind Darkest Red and Cormorant Rock, and despite the redistribution note, the consistent placed form at this distance band is the most relevant angle; the STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means he needs others to set it up for him, which in this shape is unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: Third Jim Boyle runner, prominent-style, with a placed effort at 1m2f on AW and decent recent form of 855493 — should be able to contest a prominent berth just behind Shirakawa, but the AW-heavy profile and overall handicap mark of OR=45 represent the ceiling here.|

races.paceDynamic: Shirakawa is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner handicap over 1m4f on Good To Soft ground at Epsom, and with no genuine rival to press for the lead, Callum Hutchinson can dictate terms at a sustainable, metronomic gallop that plays directly into Shirakawa's strengths. Blue Hill, Time To Sparkle and Cormorant Rock are the prominent types most likely to track closely, forming a small chasing group behind a single pace-setter — the overall tempo will be controlled rather than pressured, meaning there will be no dramatic pace collapse in the straight. The field carries a heavy load of hold-up horses — Tenison, Eze Sur Mer, Caraway, Darkest Red, Antiquarian, Eshowe, Dijon Gone and Fletcher have all been redistributed because the map cannot physically place this many true closers at the rear; of those, Caraway (Haggas, Cieren Fallon), Tenison and Darkast Red have the form and class to still get competitive positions from mid-division, but they are not racing in their true roles. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a controlled, unchallenged pace on soft ground over a staying trip — strongly favours horses racing prominently and those mid-division runners with the stamina to sustain a late run, while true deep closers who need a strong early gallop to set up their finish are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shirakawa Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Shirakawa leads uncontested from the outset and Hutchinson dictates an honest but manageable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Shirakawa sets every fraction on his own terms, the field strings out behind him from halfway, and only a horse with genuine class advantage can reel him in late on soft ground — Blue Hill and Time To Sparkle are best positioned to mount any challenge from prominent ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace means Blue Hill or Time To Sparkle can creep closer in the straight and outfinish Shirakawa over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A modest gallop allows the second and third-placed horses to travel within striking distance without spending energy, and the uphill finish at Epsom rewards those who have conserved momentum rather than chased hard from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Caraway or Tenison, despite being redistributed from their natural hold-up berth, manage to secure a tracking mid-division position and produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A gallop controlled by Shirakawa will not be strong enough to fully stretch the field, so a horse of Caraway's calibre — two second-place finishes on similar ground and trained by Haggas with Fallon aboard — can make ground without needing a true stamina test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Deep Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow increases sharply in the final half-mile, stringing out the field and enabling true hold-up horses to sweep through late.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires horses like Darkest Red, Dijon Gone or Fletcher to find clear runs through a 17-runner field from genuinely deep positions — structurally unlikely given the controlled pace shape and the redistribution of so many of these types away from their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Shirakawa holds a structural edge that no other runner possesses — if Hutchinson rolls along unchallenged at the front from the jump, this becomes a genuine test for any closer to overhaul him on soft ground over 1m4f at Epsom.

Caraway and Fallon are worth tracking from mid-division — despite being displaced from a true hold-up position, Haggas's horse has the class and ground form to make a forward move from halfway, and Fallon will find room wherever it exists in a big field.

Blue Hill and Time To Sparkle are the two prominent types most likely to pressurise Shirakawa in the final quarter-mile — if either creeps closer at the top of the hill, they will be the ones to beat the leader, not the closers.

With 17 runners and multiple redistributed hold-up horses all seeking clear runs in the straight simultaneously, traffic problems from the 2f pole are a real possibility — horses drawn wide and able to swing wide into the straight (Cormorant Rock, Time To Sparkle) may have a positional advantage purely through avoiding the scrum.

Eshowe has no turf form and all three career runs have ended in double-figure finishes on artificial surfaces — flagged for fading and with a redistribution note, this runner is a significant layering risk for exotic bets if it drifts into forecasts.

races.name: Business Pilot Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Arbaawy
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for John Butler who has placed four times in five starts but never at this trip — the step up to 1m½f is the key unknown, and his good-ground form (0 wins, 2 places from 4 similar-going runs) does not scream soft specialist; Conor Whiteley's claim is useful but he will need a stronger gallop than Wild Dahlia is likely to supply.

runners_data.name: Wild Dahlia
runners_data.note: Haggas and Fallon is a powerful combination and she has the race to herself at the front, but her going record flags a concern — only 2 runs on similar ground, 0 wins, 0 places — and she is flagged as racing out of role as a front-runner, a style shift that must be respected; if she can control the tempo, she is dangerous, but her soft-ground form does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Harry Vigors' 5lb claim softens the burden for Ollie Sangster's filly, who has placed once in three similar-ground starts and whose best effort came at 9f; stepping back up to 12f is consistent with her stamina profile, though her overall form line of 104244 shows inconsistency and she has never won beyond a mile.

runners_data.name: Eastern Veil
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo has been absent 122 days — the longest layoff in the field — which is a significant flag, but her sole turf win came over a mile and she has placed twice on Tapeta at that trip; she is a genuine prominent-style horse and her form on standard going is better than soft, so the surface is a mild query despite Balding's strong 14-day stats.

runners_data.name: Island Bear
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has the profile of a horse who has failed to win in seven starts, including three on soft or good-to-soft going without success; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes over and the trainer combination is lightly raced over the last 14 days, though the horse's consistency at around a mile-and-a-quarter suggests the step to 1m½f on soft ground is a further test he may not relish.

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Recent course-winner at a mile for Michael Bell with Hector Crouch, whose form line 836421 shows sharp improvement — two of his three placed efforts came on soft or good-to-soft ground, underlining he handles conditions; the trip is a genuine question mark as all his form is at a mile, and he may find 1m½f stretching his stamina on a soft surface.

runners_data.name: Likeness
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's consistent claimer — four of his five runs have produced a place at a mile on good or standard — is a natural hold-up horse whose instinct is to come from the rear, but in this pace-light field he has been mapped to midfield where he is unlikely to operate at his best; the form figures of 22-452 show quality without a win and his soft-ground exposure is limited to one run on standard ground.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's progressive 3yo arrives on the back of a remarkable form line (821132) with three wins in his last four and genuine versatility in terms of running style — he is a hold-up horse by nature but his willingness to race prominently means he could push forward here; soft ground is not proven for him (0 wins, 1 place from 3 similar-going runs) and Rhys Clutterbuck is a relatively inexperienced rider for a key tactical role.

runners_data.name: Sail On Sailor
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's horse arrives on a rapid 10-day turnaround having recorded three wins, including two on good ground and one on good-to-soft — but his last start produced a sixth on soft ground over 10f, suggesting conditions may have caught him out; Harry Davies takes the ride and while he is a true hold-up horse by nature, his winning profile suggests he races forward when able, which could see him drift out of position in a hold-up dominated field.

runners_data.name: Fizzy Bear
runners_data.note: George Baker's lowest-rated runner (OR 58) with a modest form line of 50504, including a win that appears distant in form terms — Jack Dace's 5lb claim is the main positive but even that cannot offset the fundamental concern that this horse has been well beaten in its last four starts and faces rivals rated up to 17lbs superior; a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield, he is likely to need a significant career-best to factor.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Dahlia is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the outset, she is set to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this mile-and-a-half on good-to-soft ground at Epsom. Eastern Bear and Island Bear are prominent types who may try to sit just off her, but with Wild Dahlia's connections (Haggas, Fallon) likely to use that uncontested lead tactically, the pace is expected to be measured rather than searching. The field is unusually hold-up heavy — Likeness, My Old Mate, Sail On Sailor, and Fizzy Bear are all true hold-up horses redistributed to a midfield mapping because they simply cannot all settle at the rear in a 10-runner race; of these, Sail On Sailor and My Old Mate are most likely to actually secure a forward position given their recent win-form and natural energy. A controlled tempo on soft ground at a flat track favours horses that can travel prominently, make their move at the top of the straight, and sustain it — the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile is best placed, while pure hold-up horses face a stiff challenge if the pace is insufficient to string the field out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Dahlia sets a steady, uncontested gallop and prominent/stalking horses travel sweetly into the straight before quickening.
scenarios.body: Wild Dahlia's controlled pace means the race is run on her terms, but the lack of genuine pressure allows horses tracking her in the first three or four to conserve energy and unleash a strong run in the Epsom straight; on good-to-soft ground this distance suits a horse with tactical speed over a true stayer's stamina. Eastern Veil and Royal Bodyguard, both capable of sitting prominently and quickening, are ideally positioned for this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Dahlia produces a career-best front-running display and the pace is slow enough that no closer can close the gap.
scenarios.body: With no rival pressing her, Wild Dahlia could steal enough of a break turning in that pursuers never quite reel her in on a flat track where leaders can sustain momentum; William Haggas's strong 13/52 14-day strike rate signals the yard is firing and Cieren Fallon will exploit the lack of pressure ruthlessly. This shape suits Wild Dahlia most obviously, with Eastern Veil perhaps the closest threat from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos In Midfield, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses, the field bunches, and genuine hold-up horses thread through a wall of tired rivals late.
scenarios.body: A truly slow early gallop could cause traffic problems for the redistributed hold-up horses — Likeness, Sail On Sailor, and My Old Mate — who find themselves hemmed in midfield rather than in their preferred rear position; however, if gaps appear in the straight, a horse with a strong late kick on soft ground could pounce, though this shape is less likely given how few true closers are in a natural hold-up position. Arbaawy and Mayaada, both consistent hold-up horses with soft-ground form, are the best candidates if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Strings Out
scenarios.trigger: If a secondary runner forces the pace unexpectedly, creating a proper test of stamina on soft ground that suits only the most resolute stayer.
scenarios.body: Should Island Bear or My Old Mate push forward and increase the tempo against Wild Dahlia, the race becomes a genuine stamina test that could expose horses without the requisite mile-and-a-half credentials on soft going; Royal Bodyguard's recent winning form at a mile might leave it vulnerable in this scenario, while Mayaada's soft-ground experience over 12f becomes more relevant. This is the lowest-probability shape given how few genuine pacemen are in the field.

watchPoints.text: Wild Dahlia (Haggas/Fallon) sets the tempo alone — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable clip, she could steal enough first-run advantage turning into the Epsom straight to hold on, making her the key shape-setter to monitor from the off.

Eastern Veil returns from a 122-day absence for Andrew Balding — if she shows signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages or drops out tamely, the pace dynamic and competitive order shift significantly; conversely, if she travels sweetly off the front-runner, she becomes the most dangerous stalker in the race.

My Old Mate and Sail On Sailor are hold-up horses likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield — watch whether either pushes forward to challenge Wild Dahlia for a prominent position, because if they do, the gallop accelerates sharply and the race shape transforms entirely.

Royal Bodyguard is unproven beyond a mile — watch how he travels in the final two furlongs, as any sign of the trip finding him out will confirm the trip is his ceiling and redirect attention to the hold-up horses finishing past him.

Fizzy Bear (OR 58, Jack Dace 5lb claim) is the outsider of the party — if he jumps well and flukes a prominent position, he could complicate the pace picture briefly, but his form makes him essentially a non-factor unless the race completely falls apart.

races.name: Feeling Flush With Emplas Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for the Moore yard who handles soft well (2 places from 15 similar-going runs), returns after just 10 days which is a slight flag; the tongue-tie is notable and the 12f trip is a career-best ask, but a strongly-run race suits his style if it materialises.

runners_data.name: Mr Ubiquitous
runners_data.note: Prominent racer dropping back to handicap company for Eustace after a spell; only one placing from 15 runs in similar going conditions is a concern, but he has form over the trip and Kaiya Fraser's booking suggests the yard is hopeful on this longer distance.

runners_data.name: I Am Me
runners_data.note: Fallon takes the ride on this Murphy-trained 4-year-old who has solid AW form at 8f but all five recent runs have been on Tapeta or Polytrack — the switch to Good To Soft turf is the primary unknown and must be respected despite his prominent style suiting the race shape.

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field with three wins on soft or similar and an active 10-day turnaround for Simon Dow who fires two winners from eight recent runners; the headgear (hood) is already in use and controlling an uncontested lead at 1m½f on this ground is a genuine proposition.

runners_data.name: Marsh Benham
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type for Baker who has placed on good-to-soft before and returns 18 days fresh; form figures of 2164 suggest a consistent if not spectacular profile, and his best chance rests on a stamina test developing from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Post Rider
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse fitted with blinkers whose best recent runs have come over 8f in similar conditions, but the step up to 1m½f is a significant stretch on his form profile; the 3lb claim from Paetel helps marginally on a mark of 68.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: Lightly-burdened 4-year-old prominent racer in good nick — two wins in the last five, both on good or soft-ish ground — with Donagh Murphy's 5lb claim reducing the weight attractively; the 10-day turnaround for Boyle, who has a live record at present, makes this a horse to respect in the prominent-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Redredrobin
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose natural instinct is to come from the rear of the field; placed twice from five runs on soft going, which is the positive angle, but this crowded hold-up division means he is unlikely to settle as far back as he prefers, which tempers confidence in his finishing effort landing at the right moment.

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: Boyle's second runner is also a genuine hold-up type by inclination, sharing the same crowded rear-of-field issue as Redredrobin; his form figures of 656336 reflect a horse looking for the right setup, and racing in a position that is not his natural one further dilutes his prospects in a race where his style-fit is already compromised.

races.paceDynamic: Tronido is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good To Soft ground at Epsom over 1m½f, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable rather than suicidal gallop — his three wins in similar conditions underline he can control tempo and still finish. Mr Ubiquitous, I Am Me, and Play Me will press forward from the prominent berths, creating a competitive early order without a true pace duel, which should keep sectionals honest but not destructive. The hold-up brigade of Oj Lifestyle, Marsh Benham, and Post Rider will track from further back, but with Redredrobin and Dandy Khan — both natural hold-up horses — repositioned into midfield because the rear of the field is overcrowded, genuine late closers will have less space and competition for a clear run than the map implies. This race shape, with a single composed front-runner setting a measured tempo on soft ground over a flat mile and a half, strongly favours prominent racers who travel within themselves and peak late into the straight rather than deep closers, who face a compromised trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tronido Dictates, Prominent Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Tronido leads uncontested at a comfortable clip and the prominent trio fail to seriously disrupt his rhythm.
scenarios.body: Tronido controls from the front on ground he handles well, and a prominent horse travelling fluently in second or third position collects as the pace inevitably steadies in the straight; the soft surface rewards those who conserve energy early and attack late from a handy pitch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Slog, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the Good To Soft conditions deteriorate the pace to a grind and stamina rather than tactical speed becomes decisive.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn tempo sees the race turn into an endurance test from the home turn, rewarding runners with the most proven bottom on this type of ground over the trip; Tronido's soft-ground win record becomes more relevant and Marsh Benham's consistent placing profile could be realised.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the straight and horses coming from off the pace deliver a late flourish.
scenarios.body: Oj Lifestyle and Post Rider, both genuine hold-up types with the ability to finish strongly, would be the primary beneficiaries of a race that falls apart in front; however, with Redredrobin and Dandy Khan occupying the same part of the track but racing out of their true role, traffic and interference risks are elevated.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Falls Over
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves surprisingly hot and Tronido ties up, leaving the race wide open in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish could produce an unexpected winner from any position, but given that the redistributed hold-up horses are not truly racing from their preferred station, the beneficiaries are most likely to be the prominent types who had been travelling kindly through the race.

watchPoints.text: Tronido (Tyler Heard) sets off from stall position unchallenged — if he gets a clean break and builds a lead before the first turn, his soft-ground front-running record makes him the primary danger to any race shape other than Scenario A.

Redredrobin and Dandy Khan are both natural hold-up horses forced into midfield — watch for crowding and traffic problems on the home turn as this cluster of runners in similar positions creates a congestion risk in the straight.

I Am Me switches from all-weather to Good To Soft turf for the first time in her recent career — if the ground is testing enough to expose that inexperience, Cieren Fallon may find her struggling to reproduce her AW form figures.

Play Me's 10-day turnaround and the combination of a 5lb claim from Murphy and Boyle's current trainer strike-rate make this runner one to track in the market — any shortening from morning prices would be significant given the prominent style suits.

The going report consistently shows Good To Soft for this race rather than the declared Soft — if the strip is riding quicker than anticipated, Tronido's advantage as a specialist soft-ground front-runner is marginally reduced and prominent types with better good-ground form, like Mr Ubiquitous, could be upgraded.
